skill.name: peer-review
skill.description: Guides structured peer review for scientific manuscripts, grants, and presentations with checks for methods, statistics, reproducibility, ethics, reporting standards, and constructive feedback.
skill.summary: Checklist-based scientific peer review for manuscripts, grants, and presentations.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

content.value_statement: Scientific reviews need structured, defensible critique across methods, statistics, ethics, and reporting. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through checklist-based reviews with constructive feedback.
actual_capabilities: Guides section-by-section manuscript review for abstracts, methods, results, discussion, references, and figures.
Checks methodological rigor, statistical reporting, sample size justification, controls, randomization, and missing data handling.
Maps reviews to reporting standards such as CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, ARRIVE, MIAME, and MINSEQE.
Structures feedback into summary statements, major comments, minor comments, and questions for authors.
Supports grant proposal and presentation review, including slide-by-slide visual feedback after image conversion.
Promotes constructive tone, balanced critique, reproducibility checks, ethics review, and actionable revision requests.
limitations: It does not verify scientific facts unless supporting documents or data are provided.
It cannot replace journal policy, editor judgment, or domain expert review.
It may need additional discipline context for specialized methods or standards.
Presentation review depends on readable slide images or successful PDF conversion.

use_cases.title: Journal Manuscript Review
use_cases.description: Prepare a structured review with major comments, minor comments, and a recommendation tied to manuscript evidence.

use_cases.title: Grant Proposal Evaluation
use_cases.description: Assess significance, innovation, feasibility, rigor, risks, and missing details before a panel discussion.

use_cases.title: Pre-Submission Quality Check
use_cases.description: Identify reporting, statistics, reproducibility, ethics, and presentation gaps before submitting research work.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Manuscript Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single manuscript.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this manuscript for major strengths, major concerns, and publication readiness. Focus on methods, statistics, reproducibility, and clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Checklist-Based Journal Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured review for a journal form.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this journal scope and manuscript text to write a structured review. Include a summary, major comments, minor comments, and author questions.

prompt_templates.title: Grant Proposal Evaluation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a proposal or application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this grant proposal for significance, innovation, feasibility, methods, risks, and reviewer-facing weaknesses. Separate essential fixes from optional improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Presentation Review From Slide Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these slide images for scientific content, readability, layout, accessibility, and timing. Give slide-specific issues and a final recommendation.

output_examples.input: Manuscript with unreported sample size justification and multiple uncorrected statistical tests.
output_examples.output: The review flags inadequate power justification, asks for multiple-testing correction, and recommends confidence intervals with effect sizes.

output_examples.input: Systematic review draft missing a protocol registration and PRISMA flow information.
output_examples.output: The output identifies reporting gaps, requests protocol details, and asks authors to clarify study selection and quality assessment.

output_examples.input: Slide deck with small figure labels and crowded results slides.
output_examples.output: The feedback lists slide-specific readability issues, recommends larger labels, and suggests simplifying overloaded results slides.

best_practices: Provide the full manuscript, venue requirements, study type, and any reviewer form before starting.
Ask for prioritized major and minor comments so authors can act on the review.
Check the recommendation against the stated evidence before sending the final review.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad extra experiments without explaining why they are necessary.
Do not mix personal style preferences with issues that affect validity or clarity.
Do not use the skill to produce confidential reviews for people who should not access them.

faq.question: What documents should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the manuscript, figures, supplementary files, journal guidance, and any review form. Add discipline and deadline details if relevant.

faq.question: Can it review grants?
faq.answer: Yes. It can assess significance, innovation, feasibility, rigor, risks, and reviewer-facing weaknesses in proposals.

faq.question: Does it check reporting standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for standards such as CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, ARRIVE, MIAME, and MINSEQE.

faq.question: Can it review presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review slide images for scientific content, layout, readability, accessibility, and timing.

faq.question: Will it make a publication decision?
faq.answer: It can recommend accept, revise, or reject based on supplied criteria. Editors or program officers make final decisions.

faq.question: Is it suitable for blinded review?
faq.answer: Yes, but remove identifying details you should not share. Follow the journal or funder confidentiality policy.
